title: Power Imbalance in Contracts Involving Small Businesses
what_it_is: Power Imbalance in Contracts Involving Small Businesses

sections.label: SMEs in Singapore economy
sections.summary: SMEs make up 99% of enterprises, employ two-thirds of the workforce and account for half of Singapore's GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In last year’s Budget, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) were described in some materials published by the Ministry of Finance as being at the heart of the Singapore economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They make up 99% of our enterprises, employ two-thirds of our workforce and account for half of Singapore’s gross domestic product.

sections.label: SMEs facing rising business costs
sections.summary: A business survey found 72.3% of SME respondents face higher business costs, up from 62.3% the year before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The same business survey also revealed that SMEs continue to face rising business costs, with 72.3% of respondents saying that they face higher business costs, compared with 62.3% the year before.

sections.label: Large players and small businesses
sections.summary: Dominant players' use of market power and unfair terms raises risks and costs for small businesses, including in rental markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: These dominant players’ usage of market power to drive the use of one-sided and unfair terms has the effect of increasing business risks and costs on the part of small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I respectfully suggest that the time has come for regulatory and legislative solutions to be offered to protect the interests of small businesses from such domineering practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In the Budget debate last year, I raised the issue of large players taking advantage of their size in commercial dealings with small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: This persists in the rental markets which involved, on the one hand, landlords with muscle, such as real estate investment trusts and, on the other hand, tenants which are small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: For example, a “demolition clause” allows the landlord to recover the premises for redevelopment purposes initiated by the landlord itself without any compensation to the tenant, who may have spent a significant sum to retrofit the premises and who may not have had the benefit of most of the terms of the tenancy.

sections.label: Illusory option to renew
sections.summary: In both cases the tenant's option to renew is effectively illusory and non-enforceable as essential renewal terms were not agreed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In both cases, the contractual provision giving the tenant the right of an option to renew is effectively illusory and non-enforceable as the essential terms for the renewed lease have not been agreed on and the tenant can potentially be provided with the Hobson's choice by the landlord at the point of renewal.

sections.label: General protection for small businesses
sections.summary: The speaker prefers examining a general protection approach like the Australian ACL over a sectoral approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Having regard to the approach taken by other countries, I personally prefer that we examine whether there is a need for a general protection approach, such as that provided by the Australian ACL, instead of a sectoral approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: This would be consistent with instilling principles of fair dealing in corporate cultures, where customers are able to have the confidence that they deal with companies where fair dealing is central to the corporate culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Such fair dealing guidelines have already been implemented in 2013 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) in the financial industry in Singapore in respect of financial institutions and their customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Providing legislative and regulatory protection for small businesses would go a long way to equalising the bargaining positions between small and large businesses and lower the business risks and costs assumed by these small businesses.

sections.label: Free-market principles in Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore's underlying philosophy is that free-market principles generally apply and Government intervenes only when necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In Singapore, our underlying philosophy is that, in general, free-market principles should apply and the Government should intervene only when necessary, for example, to address systemic market failures.

sections.label: Legislation market distortion risk
sections.summary: Enacting such legislation in Singapore can cause market distortion and eventually market inefficiency, to the detriment of all.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Enacting such legislation in Singapore can cause market distortion and, eventually, market inefficiency, to the detriment of all.

sections.label: Government landlords tenancy agreements
sections.summary: Government landlords like the Housing and Development Board and JTC have sought to ensure their tenancy agreements do not contain onerously one-sided clauses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For one, Government landlords like the Housing and Development Board and JTC have sought to ensure that their respective tenancy agreements do not contain onerously one-sided clauses.

sections.label: SME grants and cost support
sections.summary: SMEs can tap schemes like SPRING Singapore's Capability Development Grant to defray up to 70% of qualifying cost, and the Government provides near-term support such as corporate income tax rebate and Wage Credit Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For example, SMEs can tap on schemes, such as SPRING Singapore's Capability Development Grant, to defray up to 70% of qualifying cost when they embark on projects to develop their capabilities in 10 key areas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In addition, the Government provides near-term support for SMEs to manage their business costs, such as the corporate income tax rebate and Wage Credit Scheme.

sections.label: SME bargaining and Industry Transformation Maps
sections.summary: SMEs can work with trade associations to spearhead discussions with landlords and leverage the Fair Tenancy Framework, and Industry Transformation Maps have been launched to help businesses transform and grow.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To strengthen their bargaining position, SMEs can also consider working with their respective trade associations to spearhead discussions with landlords, and leverage the Fair Tenancy Framework to level the playing field for themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have also launched the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs), a collaborative effort between the Government, Trade Associations and Chambers, and industry, to help our businesses transform and grow.
